conventions.convention: ω=e^(iπ/4), O=Z[ω], and D=O[1/2]; exact coefficients use the power basis 1,ω,ω²,ω³ with ω⁴=-1. Canonical dyadic numerators have minimal nonnegative denominator exponent, with a separate zero encoding.
Bullet sends ω to -ω, fixes i, negates √2, and commutes with complex conjugation; it is distinct from complex conjugation.
For nonzero z, sde(z) is the least integer k with (√2)^k z in O; negative exponents are allowed. sde(0)=-∞. The synthesis statistic is sde(|U00|²), whose base regime is at most 3.

H and T retain their displayed exact phases; CNOT is control-first. Chronological gates multiply with later gates on the left. Scalar Clifford phases remain in exact matrices even when their resource cost is zero.
Rz approximation is ancilla-free and uses the on-the-nose operator-norm inequality. T-count counts T and T† occurrences; a free scalar Clifford phase still affects feasibility.

The efficient iterator uses ideal exact-real arithmetic and comparisons, random order within each exact-denominator layer, and a deterministic exhaustive background scan. Arithmetic-operation bounds do not imply bit-time bounds for arbitrary real inputs.

A capped prospective prime attempt accepts only an exactly checked norm certificate. Aborts, malformed operations, negative prospective outcomes, and cap exhaustion produce FACTOR_TIMEOUT, not NO_SOLUTION.

Probabilistic near-optimality and runtime use the explicit idealized independent prime-indicator model and uniform probability lower bound in A1, together with fresh independent solver bits. Actual fixed-input primality is not randomized by iterator coins. Feasible determinant-one solutions are equivalent exactly when their upper-left entries agree.

load_bearing.statement: For a unit column (u,v) over D with s=sde(|u|²)>3, some k∈{0,1,2,3} makes sde(|(u+ω^(-k)v)/√2|²)=s-1. Every such column with s≤3 is prepared exactly from |0⟩ by an H,T,T† word.

Every word has a resource-nonincreasing exact reduction with odd interior diagonal exponents. A reduced word with h≥2 has sde(|U00|²)=h+1; with h=1 the exponent is 2, and with h=0 the squared entry is 0 or 1. Reduced words minimize H count up to global phase.
A matrix U∈U(2) is exactly the matrix of a finite one-qubit Clifford+T word if and only if all four entries of U lie in D.

Z[√2] and Z[ω] are norm-Euclidean unique factorization domains with effective gcd and associate tests. Finite-search factorization in Z[ω] terminates. The units of Z[√2] are ±(1+√2)^j, and its totally positive units are exactly its unit squares, with effective square-root recovery.
For every ξ∈Z[√2,1/2] there is a terminating exact algorithm deciding whether t†t=ξ has a solution t∈D and returning one when it exists. No polynomial runtime bound is asserted.

Given ξ∈Z[√2,1/2] and a valid complete rational-prime factorization of its nonzero reduced norm numerator, an exact randomized solver returns a solution or correctly reports none, terminates almost surely, and has expected bit cost polynomial in the explicit input length. For bounded grid residuals with prime or zero/unit numerator, the specified implementation has expected cost at most 2^200(h+1)^20.

For the stated normalized positive definite ellipse matrices with eigenvalues in [H^(-1),H], a constructive lattice-preserving map simultaneously makes both ellipses at least 1/6 upright, with the stated logarithmic arithmetic and integer-part counts and polynomial entry bounds.

The iterator enumerates every simultaneous cap/disk grid point exactly once in increasing least denominator exponent. Startup costs O(L²); a layer with N solutions has O(N+1) proposals, expected polynomial prefix cost, all fixed prefix-work moments, and finite completion for every random-bit sequence.

For the displayed SU(2) matrix over D with common least nonnegative entry denominator exponent k>0, each of U and TUT† has optimal T-count in {2k-2,2k}, and their minimum is max(0,2k-2). If k=0, both counts are zero.

For c=|1-e^(iπ/8)|, every feasible exact Clifford+T matrix has determinant one when 0<ε<c. When ε≥c, a determinant-one zero-T Clifford meets the bound. Thus the minimum T-count is attained among determinant-one matrices for every positive precision.
For θ∈R, 0<ε<1/2 and U=[[u,-conj(t)],[t,conj(u)]]∈SU(2), ||Rz(θ)-U||op≤ε if and only if Re(e^(iθ/2)u)≥1-ε²/2.
Under the stated joint-failure product bound and p_j≥c/(k_j+1), the first-success index is almost surely finite, has every fixed rth moment O((k₂+1)^r), and has expected log₂ index O(1+log log(1/ε)).

concerns.concern: Fact F4 restates lem-qc-dyadic-cyclotomic-unit-circle as 'the unit elements of D are exactly ω^j'. As a ring-unit assertion this is false: 2 is a unit of D with inverse 1/2 and is not an eighth root of unity. The cited lemma requires z·conj(z)=1. Step 2.1 does establish that required modulus-one hypothesis for λ, so this finding concerns the overstrong stated fact rather than a counterexample to the characterization theorem.

Remarks say the example does not rely on 'the still-escalated converse theorem'. The current converse is supplied by thm-qc-single-qubit-exact-clifford-t-characterization and its local descent/base proof. The mathematical independence claim is correct, but the escalation-status wording is stale.

The source reference labels arXiv:1206.5236 as 'Practical approximation of single-qubit unitaries by single-qubit quantum circuits'. The linked paper is [Fast and efficient exact synthesis of single qubit unitaries generated by Clifford and T gates](https://arxiv.org/html/1206.5236). The mismatched title also occurs in several assigned arithmetic and gate items, including lem-qc-dyadic-coefficient-encoding, def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library, and lem-qc-clifford-t-entry-ring.

seams_checked.note: The determinant-one density lemma uses projective density of exact H,T words and explicitly recovers determinant-one representatives; normalized-lift phases are not treated as free controlled operations.
Gate embeddings preserve ordered wire tuples, chronological output multiplies later gates on the left, and resource coordinates remain separately declared.
The phase-equivalence definition and global-phase-under-control identity are used with their exact scalar and control-first conventions.
Controlled access remains explicit; C(T) is the control-first block operator. The no-ancilla obstruction and clean-ancilla construction do not infer controlled access from an ordinary gate call.
The exact H,S,T matrices, Pauli signs, and Rz(θ)=diag(e^(-iθ/2),e^(iθ/2)) agree with their suppliers.
The controlled-T construction uses the stated Toffoli action and restores its explicitly initialized clean work bit. The reference extension preserves the supplier's exact clean-return contract.

Inspected gate-library uses in EQP/ZQP definitions, Boolean embedding, classical containments, and Simon sampling. They use the exact fixed matrices; the Boolean compiler supplies its own explicit Toffoli replacement and charges its scratch wire.

The full-list encoding explicitly restricts labels to H,T,T†,CNOT and retains control-first order and algebraic entries. Phase-invariance and amplification uses do not import the conditional Rz runtime theorem.

Rewrite rules use exact H², T⁸, inverse-T, and same-support CNOT identities. Optimization fixes its alphabet and cost coordinate; the simulation cites only the H/CNOT matrices and separately defines its additional gate.

The page requires this synthesis page as context, but its listed item bodies contain no direct citation to an assigned batch-13 item. Its prose preserves the distinction between exact continuous-angle synthesis and finite-alphabet approximation.
